proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For each arm \(a\) and fold \(k\), and for \(d_a(x)>0\), put
\[
p_{a,J_n}(x;\alpha,\beta)
=\exp\!\left\{\alpha\log d_a(x)+\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}\beta_jB_{j,J_n}(x)\right\}.
\]
At the single chart endpoint \(d_a(x)=0\), set
\(p_{a,J_n}(x;\alpha,\beta)=e^{-J_n}\).  Let
\[
\Theta_{a,J_n}
=\left\{(\alpha,\beta)\in[0,J_n]\times[-J_n,J_n]^{J_n}:
p_{a,J_n}(x;\alpha,\beta)\le 1-e^{-J_n}
\text{ for every }x\text{ with }d_a(x)>0\right\}.
\]
Define \((\widehat\alpha_{a,-k},\widehat\beta_{a,-k})\) as the unique maximizer over \(\Theta_{a,J_n}\) of
\[
\sum_{i\notin I_k}
\left[
\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\log p_{a,J_n}(X_i;\alpha,\beta)
+\{1-\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\}
\log\{1-p_{a,J_n}(X_i;\alpha,\beta)\}
\right]
-e^{-J_n}\left(\alpha^2+\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}\beta_j^2\right),
\]
and set \(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)=p_{a,J_n}(x;\widehat\alpha_{a,-k},\widehat\beta_{a,-k})\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The present global constraint \(p_a(x)\in(0,1)\) excludes every \(\alpha>0\) candidate at the unique point where \(d_a=0\), so it forces the fitted boundary exponent to be zero. It also does not specify an attained maximizer on separated samples. The corrected compact, endpoint-safe, deterministically ridged construction is an explicit sample map and retains the intended polynomial-order likelihood problem.

proposed.name: Boundary-adapted cross-fitted Bernoulli series learner
proposed.construction:
For each arm \(a\) and fold \(k\), and for \(d_a(x)>0\), put
\[
p_{a,J_n}(x;\alpha,\beta)
=\exp\!\left\{\alpha\log d_a(x)+\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}\beta_jB_{j,J_n}(x)\right\}.
\]
At the single chart endpoint \(d_a(x)=0\), set
\(p_{a,J_n}(x;\alpha,\beta)=e^{-J_n}\).  Let
\[
\Theta_{a,J_n}
=\left\{(\alpha,\beta)\in[0,J_n]\times[-J_n,J_n]^{J_n}:
p_{a,J_n}(x;\alpha,\beta)\le 1-e^{-J_n}
\text{ for every }x\text{ with }d_a(x)>0\right\}.
\]
Define \((\widehat\alpha_{a,-k},\widehat\beta_{a,-k})\) as the unique maximizer over \(\Theta_{a,J_n}\) of
\[
\sum_{i\notin I_k}
\left[
\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\log p_{a,J_n}(X_i;\alpha,\beta)
+\{1-\mathbf 1\{A_i=a\}\}
\log\{1-p_{a,J_n}(X_i;\alpha,\beta)\}
\right]
-e^{-J_n}\left(\alpha^2+\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}\beta_j^2\right),
\]
and set \(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)=p_{a,J_n}(x;\widehat\alpha_{a,-k},\widehat\beta_{a,-k})\).
inputs: the prespecified arm chart and spline dictionary
the deterministic compact probability-range and ridge rules

proposed_core_edits.reason: The construction correction introduces the observed arm indicators and basis index explicitly, so the definition's free-symbol metadata must be replaced atomically with its construction.

open_obligations.what_is_open: After applying the endpoint-safe learner correction, prove the uniform localized Fisher lower bound, score concentration, constrained random-Hessian inversion, and signed Riesz-functional expansion for the growing Bernoulli spline likelihood.
open_obligations.obstruction: As presently defined, the learner cannot fit a positive boundary exponent: \(d_a=0\) and \(\alpha>0\) imply \(p_a=0\), contrary to the global open probability-range constraint. The target is therefore false before the proposed definition correction. After that correction, the frozen core still contains no result controlling the fitted Hessian or the singular boundary coefficient, and assuming either control would assume the theorem's crux.
open_obligations.attempted: Checked feasibility of the exact constrained map, then tested the induced \(\alpha=0\) fit on the legal mixed witness. A fixed-degree polynomial norm argument on the first knot cell gives a diverging lower bound for the claimed truncated log approximation. I also retained the Hall normalization and rate-window arithmetic from the prior round.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The obstruction is already visible before any stochastic Hessian calculation.  Let \(x_a\) denote the unique chart endpoint, so \(d_a(x_a)=0\).  Under the present construction, every candidate with \(\alpha>0\) obeys
\[
p_a(x_a)=\exp\!\left\{\alpha\log 0+
\sum_{j=1}^{J_n}\beta_jB_{j,J_n}(x_a)\right\}=0.
\]
This violates the imposed condition \(p_a(x)\in(0,1)\).  Thus every feasible candidate has \(\alpha=0\), and the advertised singular boundary direction is absent.

This is not a harmless value-at-one-point issue for the asserted supremum.  On the mixed witness, \(d_1(x)=x\) and
\(\log\pi_1(x)=\alpha_1\log x-\log2\).  With \(\alpha=0\), the fitted log propensity is a polynomial of degree at most \(r\) on the first quasi-uniform knot cell \([0,c/J_n]\), for a fixed \(c>0\).  Put
\(\epsilon_n=J_n n^{-b_0}/c\), and rescale that polynomial to a degree-\(r\) polynomial \(q_n\) on \([\epsilon_n,1]\), after subtracting the constant \(\alpha_1\log(c/J_n)-\log2\).  If
\[
e_n=\sup_{\epsilon_n\le t\le1}|q_n(t)-\alpha_1\log t|,
\]
finite-dimensional norm equivalence for degree-\(r\) polynomials gives a constant \(C_r<\infty\) such that
\[
\sup_{0\le t\le1}|q_n(t)|
\le C_r\sup_{1/2\le t\le1}|q_n(t)|
\le C_r(e_n+\alpha_1\log2).
\]
Evaluation at \(t=\epsilon_n\) consequently yields
\[
e_n\ge \alpha_1|\log\epsilon_n|-|q_n(\epsilon_n)|
\ge \alpha_1|\log\epsilon_n|-C_r(e_n+\alpha_1\log2),
\]
and hence
\[
e_n\ge
\frac{\alpha_1|\log\epsilon_n|-C_r\alpha_1\log2}{1+C_r}.
\]
For \(J_n=n^\xi\) in the displayed subcritical window and \(b_0>1\), \(\epsilon_n\to0\), so this lower bound diverges.  It contradicts the claimed vanishing log-error rate.  The Hall calculation remains valid independently of this defect:
\[
t_{a,n}=(c_an)^{-1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},\qquad
h_{a,n}=(c_an)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},\qquad
\frac n{h_{a,n}}\asymp n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)}.
\]
After the endpoint-safe learner correction is applied, the unresolved mathematical step is the localized random-Hessian expansion that produces the three asserted likelihood bounds.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove sample-point uniform consistency and bounded-tail classification of the corrected constrained series fit on the explicit mixed control arm.
open_obligations.obstruction: The population generalized inverse is explicit, but the fitted fixed-rank order statistic and Hill classification require consistency of the actual constrained likelihood sample map. No frozen statement supplies that property, and the boundary-likelihood target concerns heavy lower tails rather than this bounded arm.
open_obligations.attempted: Computed the exact control propensity distribution and the first-order expansion of its generalized-inverse threshold. Then reduced every empirical conclusion to sample-point consistency and showed how that property implies scale, order-statistic, clipping, and Hill conclusions.
open_obligations.partial_result:
For the mixed witness,
\(\pi_0(x)=1-x^{3/2}/2\), and direct inversion gives
\[
F_0^\pi(t)=
\begin{cases}
0,&t\le1/2,\\
1-\{2(1-t)\}^{2/3},&1/2<t<1,\\
1,&t\ge1.
\end{cases}
\]
Therefore \(F_0^\pi(1/2+v)=4v/3+O(v^2)\), and the generalized-inverse equation
\(ntF_0^\pi(t)=1\) gives
\[
t_{0,n}=\frac12+\frac{3}{2n}+O(n^{-2}),
\qquad h_{0,n}\longrightarrow2.
\]
The remaining conclusions reduce to one concrete property of the corrected bounded-arm likelihood fit.  If its sample-point error satisfies
\[
\max_{1\le i\le n}
|\widehat\pi_{0,-k(i)}(X_i)-\pi_0(X_i)|=o_P(1),
\]
then comparison of the fitted and true empirical distribution functions, together with continuity of \(F_0^\pi\) at \(1/2\), gives \(\widehat h_{0,n}\to_P2\).  Every fixed lower order statistic of \(\pi_0(X_i)\) converges to \(1/2\), so
\[
\widehat p_{0,(\lceil\widehat h_{0,n}\rceil)}\to_P\frac12,
\qquad
\widehat b_{0,n}\to_P\frac{\vartheta_0}{2}<\frac12.
\]
The same sample-point consistency and \(k_n/n\to0\) imply that the largest \(k_n+1\) fitted inverse propensities all converge to \(2\).  Hence their Hill log-spacing average converges to zero, so \(\widehat\gamma_0\to_P\infty\) under the stated zero-denominator convention.  It follows that clipping is inactive and the drift correction is zero with probability tending to one.  What is not supplied by the frozen core is a proof of the displayed sample-point consistency for the actual corrected constrained likelihood fit.

open_obligations.what_is_open: After the corrected boundary likelihood expansion is proved, establish joint consistency of the generalized-inverse scale, intermediate Hill statistic, nested preliminary quantiles, endpoint-score ratio, and weighted density estimator, and then complete the finite-vector convex-argmin limit.
open_obligations.obstruction: The corrected score-transfer inequality controls only the local linear score and Knight curvature. The current core has no uniform likelihood control at the intermediate order \(k_n\), no bandwidth-scale result for the nested quantiles, and no weighted kernel law of large numbers for the fully empirical density. The learner is also formally defective until the proposed construction change is applied.
open_obligations.attempted: Extended the prior transfer calculation by deriving the effective tail count at the generalized-inverse threshold, the treated count at the Hill threshold, and the exact truncated second-moment order needed by the kernel estimator. These calculations verify that the stated \(k_n\) and bandwidth conditions have the right scale but do not supply the missing likelihood and empirical-process results.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Assume only for this reduction that the three conclusions of the corrected boundary-likelihood lemma have been established.  The reciprocal identity on the tail band gives, uniformly over the finite set \(\mathcal T\),
\[
\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|S^{\mathrm{fe}}_{a,n}(\tau)-S^{\mathrm{or}}_{a,n}(\tau)|
\le
C E_{a,n}h_{a,n}^{-1}
\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le M_n/h_{a,n}\}}
{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,n}}
+\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1).
\]
Hall integration and \(c_an h_{a,n}^{-\gamma_a}\to1\) show that the expectation of the normalized sum is \(O(M_n^{\gamma_a-1})\); truncation gives the same stochastic order.  Thus the right side is
\[
O_P\{E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}\}
+\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1)=o_P(1).
\]
The same Hall relation gives
\[
nF_a^\pi(1/h_{a,n})\sim h_{a,n}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Consequently a uniform relative fitted-propensity error at the sample points, plus the binomial fluctuation of this intermediate count, would imply
\(\widehat h_{a,n}/h_{a,n}\to_P1\) and
\(h_{a,n}\widehat p_{a,(\lceil\widehat h_{a,n}\rceil)}\to_P1\).

For the Hill threshold \(t_{a,k}=F_a^{\pi,-1}(k_n/n)\), the Hall expansion gives
\[
t_{a,k}\asymp(k_n/n)^{1/(\gamma_a-1)},
\qquad
E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n
\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le t_{a,k}\}\right]
\asymp k_nt_{a,k}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
This verifies that the stated condition on \(k_n\) is exactly the nonvanishing-denominator condition for the endpoint-score average.  The mark modulus then identifies its population limit as \(m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}\).  Finally,
\[
E\!\left[
\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\{\pi_a(X)\vee b_{a,n}\}^2}
\right]=O(h_{a,n}^{,2-\gamma_a}),
\]
so the frozen bandwidth condition \(h_{a,n}/(n\omega_{a,n})\to0\) is stronger than the variance condition needed by the weighted kernel numerator.  These calculations reduce all empirical centering claims to uniform likelihood control at the extreme and intermediate order statistics, consistency of the nested quantiles on the bandwidth scale, and a uniform kernel law of large numbers.  Those results do not follow from the current frozen nodes, and the present learner must first be corrected before they can be proved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the constrained cross-fitted likelihood projection expansion and empirical-clipping negligibility for every finite-variance arm under the corrected learner.
open_obligations.obstruction: Finite \(E_P[1/\pi_a(X)]\) makes the limiting Riesz score square integrable but does not itself justify inversion of the growing random Hessian or replacement of the finite-sieve Riesz projection by its limit. Those are the load-bearing steps that create the learned-propensity influence term.
open_obligations.attempted: Derived the exact Bernoulli log-link information geometry, its Riesz representer for the signed propensity functional, the resulting score, and its algebraic recombination with the oracle quantile score. Checked that the displayed bias and nonlinear-remainder orders are compatible with the frozen tuning conditions.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The required Gaussian first-stage term has an exact likelihood geometry.  For a perturbation \(g\) of the log propensity, the Bernoulli log-link score and information inner product are
\[
s_g(O)=\frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi_a(X)\}g(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)},
\qquad
\mathcal I_a(g_1,g_2)
=E_P\!\left[\frac{\pi_a(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)}g_1(X)g_2(X)\right].
\]
The derivative of the signed functional is
\(\dot L_a(g)=E_P\{m_{a,\tau}(X)g(X)\}\).  Its Riesz representer in this information geometry is
\[
r_{a,\tau}(X)=m_{a,\tau}(X)\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)},
\]
because \(\mathcal I_a(r_{a,\tau},g)=\dot L_a(g)\).  Therefore
\[
s_{r_{a,\tau}}(O)
=\frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi_a(X)\}m_{a,\tau}(X)}{\pi_a(X)}.
\]
The finite-inverse-moment assumption and \(|m_{a,\tau}|\le1\) imply
\[
E_P\{s_{r_{a,\tau}}^2\}
=E_P\!\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)^2
\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)}\right]<\infty.
\]
Thus, if \(r_{a,\tau,J_n}\) is the information projection onto the corrected likelihood sieve, density of the spline spaces gives
\(s_{r_{a,\tau,J_n}}\to s_{r_{a,\tau}}\) in \(L^2(P)\).  The likelihood projection would then yield
\[
\sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{|I_k|}{n}
\int m_{a,\tau}(x)
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)},dP_X(x)
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n s_{r_{a,\tau}}(O_i)+o_P(1).
\]
Subtracting this expression from the oracle weighted quantile score gives exactly
\[
\mathrm{IF}_a(O;\tau)=\frac1{f_a(\tau)}
\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)+
\frac{\mathbf1\{A=a\}\{\psi_{a,\tau}(Y)-m_{a,\tau}(X)\}}
{\pi_a(X)}\right].
\]
The displayed tuning restrictions have the correct arithmetic for this route:
the product approximation bias is \(O(J_n^{-2s})\), the reciprocal-likelihood quadratic remainder is \(O_P(J_n^{\alpha_a}/n)\), and the weakest local information requires \(J_n^{\alpha_a+1}\log n/n\to0\).  After multiplication by \(\sqrt n\), the first two terms vanish under the frozen conditions.  What remains unproved is precisely the constrained random-Hessian expansion that justifies the projection display for the corrected sample map, together with first-order negligibility of its empirical clip.  Neither conclusion is a consequence of finite inverse moments alone.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\), and suppress \(P\) in probability notation.  All vectors below have the finite dimension \(R=|\mathcal T|\).  We first record the deterministic scales.  If \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\), \(\text{ass:hall}\) and the definition of \(t_{a,N}\), at an arbitrary sample size \(N\), give
\[
 N t F_a^{\pi}(t)
 =Nc_at^{\gamma_a}\{1+O(t^{\rho_a})\}.
\]
For every fixed \(\epsilon\in(0,1)\), substituting
\(t=(c_aN)^{-1/\gamma_a}(1\pm\epsilon)\) makes the last display converge to
\((1\pm\epsilon)^{\gamma_a}\).  Monotonicity of \(t\mapsto tF_a^{\pi}(t)\) and the generalized-inverse definition therefore imply
\[
 t_{a,N}=(c_aN)^{-1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},
 \qquad
 H_{a,N}=h_{a,N}=(c_aN)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
For \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\), the definition gives \(H_{a,N}=\sqrt N\).

Define the oracle-centered, fully refitted arm vector
\[
 W_{N,a}^{\circ}
 =\frac{N}{\widehat H_{a,N}}
 \{\widehat q_{a,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_a\},
 \qquad
 W_N^{\circ}=(W_{N,0}^{\circ},W_{N,1}^{\circ}).
\]
Here the subscript \(N\) means that every learner, fold, threshold, preliminary quantile, drift estimate, and density estimate is recomputed from those \(N\) observations, as required by \(\text{def:vector-subsampling}\).  The armwise heavy and Gaussian conclusions assembled in \(\text{thm:joint-qte}\), together with their scale-consistency conclusions, yield
\[
 W_N^{\circ}\Rightarrow (L_0,L_1),
 \qquad
 \frac{\widehat H_{a,N}}{H_{a,N}}\longrightarrow_P1,
 \qquad a\in\mathcal A.
 \tag{2}
\]
The heavy branch is the compensated oracle-preservation expansion, and the Gaussian branch is its influence-function expansion.  Thus (2) keeps the target \(q_a\), the estimator \(\widehat q_{a,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}\), and the limiting vector \(L_a\) distinct.

We next prove the conditional complete-subsample step rather than assume it.  The expansions used in (2) supply a permutation-symmetric oracle statistic \(S_N=(S_{N,0},S_{N,1})\): on a heavy arm it is the true-propensity, population-clip compensated quantile statistic, and on a Gaussian arm it is the normalized sum of the displayed influence functions.  The same expansions state
\[
 \|W_N^{\circ}-S_N\|\longrightarrow_P0,
 \qquad
 S_N\Rightarrow (L_0,L_1).
 \tag{3}
\]
This is exactly where full refitting and the learner schedules at sample size \(N\) are used; no oracle propensity is used by the reported estimator.

Let \(g:\mathbb R^{2R}\to\mathbb R\) be bounded and Lipschitz.  For each \(m\)-subset \(b\), let \(S_b\) be the statistic \(S_m\) evaluated on the observations indexed by \(b\), and put
\[
 U_{n,m}(g)
 =\binom nm^{-1}\sum_{|b|=m}g(S_b)
 =E_B\{g(S_B)\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\}.
\]
This is a \(U\)-statistic with the symmetric kernel \(g(S_m)\).  To make its concentration explicit, center that kernel and write its orthogonal Hoeffding decomposition as
\[
 g(S_m)-E\{g(S_m)\}
 =\sum_{j=1}^m\ \sum_{C\subset\{1,\ldots,m\}:|C|=j}h_{m,j}(O_C),
\]
where each \(h_{m,j}\) is degenerate in every coordinate.  Independence in \(\text{ass:iid}\) makes distinct projection terms orthogonal.  If
\(\zeta_{m,j}=E\{h_{m,j}(O_1,\ldots,O_j)^2\}\), counting the \(m\)-subsets containing a given \(j\)-subset gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\{g(S_m)\}
 =\sum_{j=1}^m\binom mj\zeta_{m,j},
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\{U_{n,m}(g)\}
 =\sum_{j=1}^m
 \frac{\binom mj^2}{\binom nj}\zeta_{m,j}
 \le \frac mn\operatorname{Var}\{g(S_m)\}
 \le 4\|g\|_\infty^2\frac mn.
 \tag{4}
\]
The inequality uses
\(\binom mj/\binom nj\le m/n\) for \(1\le j\le m\).  Since \(m/n\to0\), (3), (4), and
\[
 E\{U_{n,m}(g)\}=E\{g(S_m)\}
 \longrightarrow E\{g(L_0,L_1)\}
\]
show that
\[
 E_B\{g(S_B)\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\}
 \longrightarrow_P E\{g(L_0,L_1)\}.
 \tag{5}
\]
A countable convergence-determining subclass of the bounded Lipschitz functions on the finite-dimensional Euclidean space turns (5) into conditional weak convergence in probability.

The feasible-to-oracle replacement also holds conditionally.  Indeed, a uniformly selected \(m\)-subset of an iid sample has the same unconditional law as \(m\) iid observations.  Hence, for every \(\epsilon>0\), (3) and iterated expectation give
\[
 E\!\left[
 P_B\{\|W_B^{\circ}-S_B\|>\epsilon\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\}
 \right]
 =P\{\|W_m^{\circ}-S_m\|>\epsilon\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Markov's inequality therefore makes the conditional probability inside brackets converge to zero in \(P\)-probability.  Combining this fact with (5) yields
\[
 \mathcal L_B(W_B^{\circ}\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n)
 \Rightarrow_P \mathcal L(L_0,L_1).
 \tag{6}
\]

It remains to justify the full-sample centering used by \(V_{B,a}\).  From \(\text{def:vector-subsampling}\),
\[
 V_{B,a}
 =W_{B,a}^{\circ}-C_{B,a},
 \qquad
 C_{B,a}
 =\frac m{\widehat H_{a,m,B}}
 \{\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_a\}.
 \tag{7}
\]
Equation (2), first at size \(n\) and then at size \(m\), implies
\[
 \|\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_a\|
 =O_P(H_{a,n}/n),
 \qquad
 \widehat H_{a,m,B}/H_{a,m}\longrightarrow1
\]
under the joint law of the data and the conditional random subset.  The same iterated-expectation and Markov argument used above converts the second relation to conditional convergence in \(P\)-probability.  Consequently (1) gives, for a heavy arm,
\[
 \|C_{B,a}\|
 =O_P\!\left(\frac m{H_{a,m}}\frac{H_{a,n}}n\right)
 =O_P\!\left\{(m/n)^{1-1/\gamma_a}\right\}
 =o_P(1),
 \tag{8}
\]
because \(\gamma_a>1\).  For a Gaussian arm the corresponding bound is
\[
 \|C_{B,a}\|=O_P\{\sqrt{m/n}\}=o_P(1).
 \tag{9}
\]
The finite arm set and \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\) make (8)--(9) simultaneous across arms.  Thus (6)--(9) prove
\[
 \mathcal L_B((V_{B,0},V_{B,1})\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n)
 \Rightarrow_P\mathcal L(L_0,L_1).
 \tag{10}
\]

Scale consistency in (2) also gives
\[
 \widehat\ell_{a,n}-\ell_{a,n}\longrightarrow_P0.
\]
Along a subsequence on which \(\ell_{a,n}\to\ell_a\), conditional Slutsky applied to (10) and the definition
\(T_{B,n}=\widehat\ell_{1,n}V_{B,1}-\widehat\ell_{0,n}V_{B,0}\) proves
\[
 \mathcal L_B(T_{B,n}\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n)
 \Rightarrow_P
 \mathcal L(\ell_1L_1-\ell_0L_0).
 \tag{11}
\]

For coverage, fix \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), and denote the scalar limit in (11) by
\(Z_\tau=\ell_1L_1(\tau)-\ell_0L_0(\tau)\).  By \(\text{ass:anti-concentration}\), its distribution is continuous at the two required quantiles.  Conditional weak convergence in (11) therefore yields
\[
 c_{n,p}(\tau)\longrightarrow_P c_p(\tau),
 \qquad p\in\{\alpha/2,1-\alpha/2\},
 \tag{12}
\]
where \(c_p(\tau)\) is the \(p\)-quantile of \(Z_\tau\).  On the other hand, \(\text{thm:joint-qte}\) and
\(\widehat H_n/H_n\to_P1\) give
\[
 \frac n{\widehat H_n}
 \{\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\Delta(\tau)\}
 \Rightarrow Z_\tau.
 \tag{13}
\]
The event that the displayed interval covers \(\Delta(\tau)\) is exactly
\[
 c_{n,\alpha/2}(\tau)
 \le \frac n{\widehat H_n}
 \{\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\Delta(\tau)\}
 \le c_{n,1-\alpha/2}(\tau).
\]
Equations (12)--(13) and continuity give limiting probability \(1-\alpha\).  Since \(\mathcal T\) is finite, the maximum of the finitely many coordinatewise coverage errors also converges to zero.

We finally prove both the failure of uniform convergence to the fixed-law limit and the raw-scalar warning.  Choose
\(1<\gamma<2\) in the interior of the heavy interval from \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\), a constant \(c>0\), and the two-heavy family certified by \(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\), with equal Hall constants and with independent nondegenerate endpoint limits \(L_0,L_1\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), set
\[
 \gamma_{0,n}=\gamma+\frac{c}{2\log n},
 \qquad
 \gamma_{1,n}=\gamma-\frac{c}{2\log n}.
 \tag{14}
\]
The associated boundary exponents stay in a compact subset of \((1,\infty)\), so the Hall, smoothness, endpoint-mark, density, positivity, and opposite-overlap conditions hold with common constants; hence the resulting laws \(P_n\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\).  Applying (1) at the row sample size \(n\) gives
\[
 \log\frac{h_{0,n}}{h_{1,n}}
 =\left(\frac1{\gamma_{0,n}}-\frac1{\gamma_{1,n}}\right)\log n+o(1)
 \longrightarrow-\frac c{\gamma^2}.
 \tag{15}
\]
Thus the row-wise full-sample law retains the mixture
\[
 L_1-e^{-c/\gamma^2}L_0.
 \tag{16}
\]
In contrast, for every fixed \(n\), if the law \(P_n\) is held fixed while a new sample size \(N\to\infty\), then
\[
 \frac{h_{0,N}}{h_{1,N}}
 \asymp N^{1/\gamma_{0,n}-1/\gamma_{1,n}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Its fixed-law limit in \(\text{thm:joint-qte}\) is therefore \(L_1\), not (16).  These two laws are different: independence gives the characteristic function of (16) as
\(\varphi_1(t)\varphi_0(-e^{-c/\gamma^2}t)\); since \(\varphi_1\) is nonzero near zero, equality with \(\varphi_1\) there would force the nondegenerate \(L_0\) to be zero almost surely.  A bounded Lipschitz function consequently separates the two laws by a positive amount.  This triangular sequence is an explicit certificate that convergence to each member's fixed-law limit cannot be uniform over \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\).

Now let \(m=n^\beta\) with \(0<\beta<1\).  The same computation as (15), still under the row law \(P_n\), yields
\[
 \log\frac{h_{0,m}}{h_{1,m}}
 =\left(\frac1{\gamma_{0,n}}-\frac1{\gamma_{1,n}}\right)\log m+o(1)
 \longrightarrow-\frac{\beta c}{\gamma^2}.
 \tag{17}
\]
A raw scalar QTE subsample therefore converges to
\(L_1-e^{-\beta c/\gamma^2}L_0\), which differs from the full-sample row mixture (16).  The arm-vector procedure avoids this error because it estimates each \(L_a\) at its own \(m\)-scale and recombines the two coordinates with the full-sample weights \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}\), whose ratio converges by (15), rather than with the \(m\)-scale ratio in (17).  This proves the final assertion.

Under \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\), \(\text{ass:anti-concentration}\), and the regular armwise learner schedules in the heavy and Gaussian claims imposed both at sample size \(n\) and after every refit at sample size \(m\), where \(m\to\infty\) and \(m/n\to0\), the following holds. \]
weakly in \(P\)-probability.  For every \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the pointwise interval
\[

The asserted uniform convergence to each law's fixed-law limit is false on a compact two-heavy triangular sequence whose index gap is of order one over log sample size: its row-wise two-arm mixture remains nondegenerate although each fixed law has a one-arm asymptotic limit.
